title: After Brazil and Serbia’s Elections
gist: A Project Syndicate Big Picture collection argues that recent electoral defeats of far-right forces in Brazil and Serbia hold lessons for pro-democracy forces confronting nationalist and illiberal movements. It cautions that no single election guarantees democratic resilience and that both new governments face formidable challenges.

insights.claim: Far-right forces were recently defeated in elections in both Brazil and Serbia, which the PS editors present as offering important lessons for pro-democracy forces confronting nationalist and illiberal movements worldwide.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: Signals a possible turning point in the populist wave with implications for EM political risk premia.
insights.quote: The recent electoral defeat of far-right forces in Brazil and Serbia offers important lessons for pro-democracy forces around the world

insights.claim: No single election can guarantee democracy's resilience, and the new governments in Brazil and Serbia face formidable challenges.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: Investors should not over-extrapolate election outcomes into lasting governance improvement.
insights.quote: But no single election can guarantee democracy’s resilience, and the challenges these countries’ new governments face remain formidable.

insights.claim: The Project Syndicate Big Picture on the Brazil and Serbia elections features commentary from Filip Milačić, Robert Muggah, Ilona Szabó de Carvalho, Jeremy Adelman and Gene Frieda.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: Includes a macro/markets contributor (Gene Frieda), suggesting market implications are addressed in the full collection.
